title: On the web device tier, a failed erase write has no put-back, so the reminders row is tombstoned and a reload brings the record back with the opt-in active
evidence: Checkpoint 4 look-back. Design note first. S57's put-back covers only the cloud tier: packages/health-core/src/record-session-erase.ts:163 (host.tier === 'cloud' && s.writtenNowhere). On the device tier (widget-src/src/storage/web-record-host.ts:185, a LocalStorageAdapter host) the flush (record-session-erase.ts:125) goes to LocalStorageAdapter.writeSync (widget-src/src/storage/local-storage-adapter.ts:133), which throws StorageError(FULL) when the record setItem fails (:158-161) or WritesStoppedError after a log-off (:140); a failed revision write (:174) may have stored the change, so a put-back there must be the definite case only. The erase then answers { success: false, error } at record-session-erase.ts:167 with the erased copy kept in memory: the swap at :113-115 has already moved the erase identity. So after PR 1674 (S59), deleteUserData (widget-src/src/lib/roadmap-data.ts:363-366) sees store.eraseIdentity !== before and runs the reminders commit, which tombstones (or deletes) the server row. Nothing erased reached localStorage, so a reload reads the pre-erase record, its reminder opt-in still active, while the row is gone; the next schedule push gets a 404 and flips the opt-in to cancelled (S59's path). Fix options for the design note: put the copy back on the device tier too when the write definitely failed (as S57 does in the cloud), or have the commit wait for a landed write on the device tier. US-11 AC2, AC4c; US-17 AC4
